Learned counsel Mr. Mahaveer Bishnoi points out that the petitioner had just been posted as the SHO of the police station shortly before the final report under Section 173 CrPC was presented.
The investigation had already been concluded by the previous Investigating Officer.
The petitioner simply presented the final report under Section 173 CrPC in the court..

He further submits that the trial court has passed strictures against the petitioner without providing him an opportunity to show case and thus, the directions given by the appellate court are contrary to the principles of natural justice and the observations/strictures made against the petitioner are liable

sentences.text:
In support of his arguments, Mr. Bishnoi has placed reliance upon this court's judgment in the case of Sumit Kumar Vs. State of Rajasthan (S.B.
Criminal Misc. Petition No.254/2014) decided on 08.07.2016.

entities.text:
Sumit Kumar Vs. State of Rajasthan (S.B.
Criminal Misc. Petition No.254/2014)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned Public Prosecutor though vehemently opposed the submissions advanced by the petitioner's counsel, but he too is not in position to dispute the fact that no notice to show cause was served upon the petitioner by the appellate court before passing the strictures against him and that he was not heard in the matter before issuing these directions.

In this background, apparently, the order passed by the appellate court, whereby the strictures referred to above were made and directions to proceed against the petitioner were issued, cannot be sustained as the same are totally contrary to the principles of natural justice.
Thus, the instant miscellaneous petition deserves to be and is hereby allowed.

The strictures referred to supra made by the appellate court [2025:RJ-JD:1892] (4 of 4) [CRLMP-3846/2021] against the petitioner at para No.22 of the judgment dated 17.03.2017 are expunged and struck off qua the petitioner."
6.
In view of the above, the instant criminal misc. petition is allowed.

The adverse comments made in Para No.44 of the order dated 02.03.2021 passed by the learned Special Sessions Judge,
Protection of of Children from Sexual Offices Act, 2012 and Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005, Bikaner in Criminal Case No.101/2018 are expunged and that shall not be taken and read as a part of that order.
7. Stay petition is disposed of.
